scope: Static native object-graph review for the archived target APK. Structural explanation and implementation eligibility design; not a device trace.

checks.finding: Copies configured popup characters, then appends nonduplicate language-specific variants obtained through jc0/b.h(primary label), preserving configured characters before appended variants.
An empty candidate list becomes xc0/d. One candidate without touch exploration becomes xc0/i. Multiple candidates become xc0/f wrapping a fully built fb0/f2 popup keyboard.

Only xc0/i enters the branch that creates fc0/d1 with d=true and registers it through hc0/b.p. The common nonempty-popup branch creates e60/b(original key state, androidx/lifecycle/h(popup,7)); its fc0/b1 opener is registered through hc0/b.q.

p registers wrapped actors in hc0/k.d (long-press release). q registers wrapped actors in hc0/k.b (long-press activation). d wraps ic0/a in ic0/e. x instead stores raw ic0/a in bf0/g.b with hc0/o restrictions.
Tag a=1 identifies the e60/b-bound opener; b stores its e60/b owner. Calling it would open the popup, so the new resolver should inspect fields only.

The popup-specific constructor stores original key state in b and constant provider in a, creates fc0/b1(this,1) in c, and ic0/w(this) in d. m invokes provider then key-state.n(popup); resolver must not call it.
Tag a=7 returns b cast to xc0/h without constructing a new popup. Inspecting a and b directly avoids invoking arbitrary provider code and preserves existing popup identity.
Public final a stores the already-built native popup keyboard fb0/f2.
Public final l is the native default candidate index; inherited fb0/f0.d contains actual popup keys. Inherited fb0/t0.b is a dummy fallback key, not the configured default candidate.
The actual popup initialization obtains the key as v.d.get(v.l). This establishes the default-selection meaning of fb0/f2.l.

Native zero-displacement popup selection also starts from fb0/f2.d[fb0/f2.l], then synthesizes its own down/up. The flick resolver need not execute this actor or synthesize events; it can reuse the selected child insertion actor.

For one row, reorders candidates as left-list + original input[0] + right-list and returns default index equal to left-list size, so the first configured character remains the selected default despite a nonzero index.

Default horizontal popup column limit k is Integer.MAX_VALUE. fc0/v1 constructor copies k to i, which controls the single-row versus multirow branch in fc0/s1.P. Custom limited layouts may use another native default placement; do not assume list index zero or all default characters always equal the visible hint.

Builds actual popup fc0/n2 keys with oc0/m handlers. Ordinary character insertion uses raw fb0/l2, registered with hc0/b.x into child handler.b:bf0/g.b. Both ordinary a and c paths pass true,true to the actor flags d/e. Label and textForPunctuation are required nonnull; text normalization is performed before actor construction.

Actor fields a=fb0/n2 factory, b=input string, c=punctuation string, d/e=native flags. Invokes factory.a:wb0/t0.b0(token,b,c,d,e). Reuse this actor rather than manufacturing fc0/d1 or committing through InputConnection.
Passes the same input-model argument p5 into fc0/k1 and fb0/n2. A resolved popup actor can be checked against the current keyboard model through fb0/l2.a.a.
Stores its input-model constructor argument in public z:wb0/t0, the model already snapshotted by FlickSymbols.

Evaluates each hc0/o restriction against the supplied current key state and returns active actor objects. Apply first to original long-press opener list, then to selected popup child release list; do not skip restrictions.

The native mini-keyboard backend clears native pending state, prepares keyboard state, and enqueues a yb0/o0 input event. It is distinct from the fc0/d1 wb0/t0.P route and should retain its own actor/flags.

fb0/h2.b registers the ordinary raw fb0/l2 release actor together with its telemetry actor via hc0/b.x under aa0/f(16). This branch checks nonnull fc0/d2 and returns Boolean.TRUE, so release actor eligibility does not require opening or pressing the popup first. Production still reevaluates hc0/o restrictions.

resolver_chain: hc0/o.a(activation list, original key.d) -> ic0/e.a -> fc0/b1 with tag a=1
fc0/b1.b -> e60/b; require binding.b == original key.d
e60/b.a -> androidx/lifecycle/h with tag a=7; read b without invoke
native default child = popup.d.get(popup.l), with bounds and type validation
child fc0/n2.b -> oc0/m.b -> hc0/a.b -> bf0/g.b restricted with child.d
raw fb0/l2 insertion actor; verify one printable character in b and c, known flags and same model owner
call retained native ic0/a.b(token) only at existing validated UP commit point
required_invariants: Preserve the existing direct single-character fc0/d1 path.
Do not create or display a popup, call a supplier or opener, synthesize DOWN/UP, or bypass the native insertion backend.
Reject unknown wrappers, wrong discriminators, wrong original-key binding, invalid default index/key, ambiguous insertion actors, invalid single-character output and foreign input-model ownership.

Preserve starting native opener/binding/provider/popup/index/child/actor identity across the gesture; re-resolve restrictions and native default selection before and after CANCEL and before UP insertion.
Retain existing gesture capture timing, movement thresholds, editor/layout/window/model protections and canceled-stream drain semantics.
Do not report key characters, popup text, surrounding text, absolute touch position or editor identity in diagnostics.
limitations: No actual runtime per-key objects or user device gesture samples were captured. The q/w/p versus e/r/t/y/u/i/o pattern is consistent with the single-versus-multiple-popup structural defect; this review alone does not prove the installed language-variant map for each user key.
The default popup selection is the native configured default, not an arbitrary first list entry or a hardcoded qwerty-to-digit mapping. Custom layouts or multirow popups can choose another default.

Single-row ordering proves the configured initial popup character survives reordering as the native default. Device-specific language/settings/layout behavior and insertion side effects still require device confirmation.

implementation_review.review_method: Independent source diff against 1.8.12 and actual decoded native object-graph/actor/backend inspection; final production source hash pinned.
checks: Existing direct fc0/d1 long-press route is preserved; fallback starts only when that restricted list contains no fc0/d1. Invalid or ambiguous direct actors are rejected instead of silently switching routes.

Fallback matches the actual ic0/e -> fc0/b1(tag 1) -> e60/b(original key state) -> androidx/lifecycle/h(tag 7) -> xc0/f -> fb0/f2 route using read-only field access. No provider or popup opener is invoked.
Native default selection is popup.d[popup.l] with null, bounds, child-type and handler checks. It does not assume first list entry, copy key labels, or hardcode letters or digits.

Child release lookup reevaluates hc0/o restrictions against child.d and resolves the actual raw fb0/l2 actor. Multiple insertion actors, wrong input-model ownership, unexpected flags, and non-single-character b/c outputs are rejected.
The fb0/l2 d/e true,true requirement matches ordinary native single-row and multirow construction. The factory input-model identity guard matches shared model construction and xd0/f0.z.

The original opener, binding, provider, popup, default index, child key and insertion actor identities are snapshotted and required to remain stable. Re-resolution runs before native CANCEL, after CANCEL and immediately before UP insertion.

Invocation remains the retained native ic0/a.b(token) at the existing validated UP point. No new insertion actor, InputConnection.commitText call, popup display or synthetic native child DOWN/UP is introduced.
Gesture distance, direction, capture timing and pointer ownership/drain behavior are unchanged from 1.8.12; only native alternate eligibility, actor interface and non-text diagnostics are extended.
Added diagnostics are counters and fixed route/rejection identifiers. No key character, popup candidate, surrounding text, absolute touch position or editor identity is added to diagnostics.
limitations: This is a static source/native audit, not execution on the user device. No actual per-key runtime candidate objects or language-variant lists were captured.
The selected output follows the native configured popup default; custom layouts with another default are not forced to match a displayed secondary hint.
Host regression tests, compiled DEX ABI verification and publishing checks are separately recorded by their owning build/test reports.
